messages:
ana: Heads up — export of hf/model-x to Redwood runtime produced unexpected token ID collisions. Seeing BOS/EOS mapped to same id after conversion.

mike: hm. can you paste the exact symptoms? is it after quantize or during tokenizer conversion?

ana: conversion pipeline: `transformers` tokenizer -> save_pretrained -> our convert_hf_to_redwood script -> load in runtime. After convert, `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(["<bos>", "<eos>"])` returns same int. Also observed some added_tokens entries with diacritics that normalize differently (NFC vs NFKC).

raja: rough guess: added_tokens.json contains both composed and decomposed unicode variants, and our normalization step merges them but then remaps ids. Did the HF tokenizer have `do_normalize=True`?

ana: HF tokenizer config shows `do_normalize: true` and `normalizer: {"type":"nfc"}`. But added_tokens.json was generated from a dataset that had NFKD outputs. So duplicates exist like "e\u0301" vs "\u00e9".

eva: that explains collisions. When we dedupe added_tokens we keep last-occurrence id mapping which can overwrite BOS/EOS if they were represented with different codepoints but same visual token. Did you check special_tokens_map.json?

ana: yes — special_tokens_map had "bos_token": "<s>" and "eos_token": "</s>" but some added_tokens included literal variants `"<s>\u2060"` (zero-width) from copy/paste. Weird.

mike: can you repro with a minimal script? If we can show conversion bug we can patch convert_hf_to_redwood to normalize added_tokens with the tokenizer's normalizer.

ana: repro gist:```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/model-x')
print('normalize:', t.init_kwargs.get('do_normalize'), t.init_kwargs.get('normalizer'))
print('special:', t.special_tokens_map)
print('added_tokens sample:', t.added_tokens_encoder.get('e\u0301', 'missing'), t.added_tokens_encoder.get('\u00e9', 'missing'))
```
I can share model metadata privately.

convert-bot: convert job 2234 started (hf/model-x -> redwood/model-x:v1).

raja: quick mitigation: before deduping, run the tokenizer normalizer on every added_token string, then dedupe using the normalized form but preserve a canonical representative that matches special_tokens_map keys. Essentially: `norm = t.normalizer.normalize_str(tok)` (pseudocode). If normalizer not present, run Unicode NFC.

ana: tried that locally: normalizing before dedupe prevents bos/eos id overwrite. But it changed token id ordering so the runtime reported `vocab_size` mismatch vs model weights (embedding matrix shape mismatch).

mike: yeah that's the follow-up — token id reorder will break embeddings if we don't also permute weights. Two options: 1) keep original id order but add new dedup map that aliases normalized tokens to existing id (no reordering), or 2) reorder and rewrite embedding matrix accordingly. For short-term, aliasing is safer.

raja: agreed. aliasing approach: when we encounter normalized duplicate, point all token lookups to the canonical id via `added_tokens_map[normalized] = existing_id` and do not change `vocab` array order. Add metadata `aliases` so runtime can map during token->id.

a na: implemented alias mapping in convert script, ran CI quant tests (INT8), and embeddings align. However, downstream decoding step produced occasional extra spaces around composed characters (token merging changed split points).

eva: that could be tokenizer split differences (pretokenizer behavior). Are you preserving tokenizer.pre_tokenizer settings and `add_prefix_space`? Many GPT-style tokenizers require add_prefix_space to be consistent.

ana: we preserved pre_tokenizer config. The decode differences are small but visible in evals — rouge/bleu delta on a probe set. Not catastrophic but flags reg.

mike: action items: 1) add normalization pass in convert that uses tokenizer's own normalizer when present, producing aliases instead of reordering; 2) add a post-conversion decode audit (small eval set) to detect splits/spacing regressions; 3) add a warning in console if special token aliases overlap with reserved ids (pad/unk/bos/eos).

raja: will open PR for aliasing & warning. Ana, can you attach a minimal failing sample (input -> expected decode -> actual decode) to the PR so QA can reproduce?

ana: attaching sample in PR. Example: input "cafe01 and cafe\u00e9" expected identical; after conversion decode yields "cafe \u0301" vs "café" (spacing).

convert-bot: convert job 2234 completed with warnings: 1) added_tokens normalization collisions; 2) aliasing applied.

eva: follow-up longer-term: consider storing added_tokens as unicode-normalized canonical forms in our model catalog and display diffs during onboarding. Also surface `vocab_size` vs embedding shape mismatches earlier in conversion pipeline.

mike: +1. Also add unit tests for combined NFC/NFKD edgecases and a small corpus with zero-width joiners.

ana: thanks all — PR up with tests and repro. Will monitor early canary. :thumbsup:
